comparison: Perfect agreement on behavioral findings (C22-C26). Both evaluations find the data robustly support distinct stinging patterns between species, with OpenEval noting quantitative statistical analysis (p<0.05, n=10-13) and peer reviewers confirming the phenomenon is 'justified by the data in Figure 1.'

Strong agreement on modeling results (C27-C32). Both evaluations support the match between Markov decision process predictions and experimental data. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative statistical significance (p<0.0001), while peer reviewers note 'qualitatively comparable' scaling and conformance to model predictions.

Complete agreement on integrative behavioral conclusions (C33-C34). Both evaluations affirm the link between stinging behavior and ecological niches. OpenEval describes convergence of multiple evidence lines, peer reviewers confirm 'precise stinging control adapted for predation' versus 'indiscriminately stings for defense.'

Full agreement on calcium dependence and electrophysiology (C35-C40). Both evaluations support pharmacological and patch clamp findings. OpenEval notes appropriate controls and sample sizes (n=3-9), peer reviewers confirm 'clearly shown by blocking respective currents' with supporting patch clamp data.

Strong agreement on differential inactivation properties (C41-C45). Both evaluations support the correlation between channel properties and behavior. OpenEval notes quantitative measurements (n=3-7) with inferential mechanistic links, peer reviewers affirm channels 'not strongly inactivated' accounting for behavioral differences.

Agreement on molecular identification of CaVβ isoforms (C46-C49), though peer R6 also covers C50-C53. OpenEval emphasizes complementary transcriptomic, ddPCR, and in situ data showing mutually exclusive expression. Peer reviewers confirm 'clean electrophysiological characterisation' and transcriptomics evidence.

Partial overlap on heterologous expression (C50-C52). OpenEval R7 focuses on distinct inactivation properties from expression experiments with quantitative data (Vi1/2 values, n=5-8). Peer R6 covers broader molecular evidence including these isoforms as 'different splice variants' producing variable inactivation.

Minimal overlap on alternative splicing (C53). OpenEval R8 specifically addresses genomic alignment evidence for N-terminus splicing. Peer R6 mentions splice variants more broadly as part of comprehensive molecular characterization but doesn't separately evaluate C53.

Strong agreement on chimeric channel experiments (C55-C57). Both evaluations support N-terminus as sufficient for transferring inactivation properties. OpenEval provides quantitative details (n=2-8, p<0.001), peer reviewers confirm 'variable N-termini are important determinants' based on chimeric analysis.

Agreement on comparative CaVβ analysis across cnidarians (C58-C62). OpenEval emphasizes multi-species approach strengthening generalizability, peer reviewers note analysis of '6 Cnidaria' to strengthen the N-terminus variation hypothesis. Peer R8 also includes C73 on evolutionary implications.

Agreement on integrative electrophysiology-behavior conclusions (C66-C68). OpenEval synthesizes electrophysiological, behavioral, modeling, and ecological data with evolutionary interpretation noted as inferential. Peer R9 covers broader conclusions including these claims as part of overarching findings.

Agreement on molecular-behavioral integration (C69-C70, C72). OpenEval synthesizes molecular, electrophysiological, behavioral, modeling, and ecological evidence. Peer R9 includes these claims within comprehensive affirmation of manuscript conclusions linking channel properties to behavior.

Agreement on evolutionary mechanism conclusions (C73-C74). OpenEval supports comparative CaVβ analysis with C74 noted as speculative but well-grounded. Peer R8 affirms 'convincing evidence' for mechanism with relevance to 'molecular basis of non-neural behavior and its evolutionary basis.'

Agreement on overarching conclusions (C83-C84). OpenEval supports broad conclusions about single protein driving behavioral diversity through comprehensive data integration. Peer R9 calls it 'an important paper' with conclusions 'in general supported by the experiments and analysis.'

Perfect agreement on prior work citations (C1, C8-C14). Both evaluations recognize these as appropriately cited background from Weir et al. 2020 and other sources. OpenEval notes they provide context, peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'The authors had previously shown' these findings.

Agreement on ecological context (C3, C16-C18, C20). OpenEval recognizes established ecological knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer R11 accepts ecological characterizations without challenge, noting comparison of 'two related anemones' with different niches. Peer R11 also covers C15, C19, C21.

Agreement on speculative nature of C54. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about functional significance with conditional language. Peer R12 groups with other speculative claims, noting reviewers 'do not directly evaluate' these explicitly speculative extensions.

Agreement on ecological speculation (C63-C65). OpenEval supports C63-C64 by citations with C65 as speculative but logically grounded. Peer R12 treats as explicitly speculative claims lacking direct experimental support, though representing reasonable inferences.

Agreement on speculative discussion (C75-C77). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, describing reasonable hypotheses for future work lacking direct experimental support. Peer R12 confirms these are 'explicitly speculative claims' that reviewers do not specifically affirm or challenge.

Agreement on cnidarian biology context (C78-C81). OpenEval recognizes general knowledge with appropriate citations providing important context. Peer R13 confirms these background claims are 'accepted as established knowledge' with extensive reviewer discussion of basal metazoan neurobiology.

Agreement on model organism utility (C82). OpenEval supports claim by citations as established knowledge about cnidarians as models. Peer R13 includes this within accepted background context, with reviewers noting cnidarians as 'exciting model organisms.'

Agreement on high-level summary statements (C2, C4-C7). OpenEval recognizes these as well-supported synthesis of main findings. Peer R9 includes these claims within comprehensive affirmation of overarching conclusions, with all reviewers supporting the integration.

Agreement on motivating hypotheses (C15, C19, C21). OpenEval supports these as logical inferences with hypothesis well-supported by subsequent results. Peer R11 accepts the ecological framework and hypothesis without challenge as appropriate study motivation.

Agreement on speculative claim (C71). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting citation-supported speculation not directly tested. Peer R12 groups with other speculative claims lacking direct experimental support but representing reasonable hypotheses for future investigation.
